title: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation:  Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
summary: Deep learning regression and classification tools typically do not capture model uncertainty, whereas Bayesian models do but at prohibitive computational cost. The paper casts dropout training in neural networks as approximate variational inference in deep Gaussian processes, yielding MC dropout: averaging T stochastic forward passes to estimate predictive mean and variance. On UCI regression benchmarks, notably Boston Housing, MC dropout improves test RMSE and predictive log-likelihood over VI and probabilistic back-propagation, achieving 2.97 ± 0.19 RMSE on Boston Housing in the 20-split setting.

text: Cloning into 'repo'...

why: The authors' repo is cloned and contains the entire experimental apparatus: experiment.py, net/net.py, and all UCI_Datasets directories with data.txt, the exact 20 train/test index splits, dropout_rates.txt, tau_values.txt, n_epochs/n_hidden configs, plus the authors' published result files (test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt etc.) for direct comparison. Nothing data- or weight-wise is missing (models are trained from scratch). What is broken is the runtime: the code targets Keras 2.2.0 on Theano 0.8.2 (README), Theano is unmaintained and not installable on Python 3.12, TF1.x/Keras 2.2 wheels do not exist for Python 3.12, and 9 of 11 Python files are Python-2 style. So we keep the authors' logic (architecture, dropout rates, epochs, tau/grid-search protocol, per-split train/val selection) but port the training/evaluation core to a modern framework and run the same splits.
est_runtime: Port work: ~20-30 min (rewrite net/net.py + experiment.py training/MC-dropout loop in a modern framework, keep split loading and grid-search logic). Runs (Boston Housing, 1x50 net, 400 epochs, batch 32, per-split grid over the repo's dropout_rates/tau_values, T MC forward passes): ~10-15 s per model fit on 22 CPU cores, so ~2-4 min per split with grid search. Full 20-split C1 protocol is ~40-80 min of compute, i.e. borderline-to-over the ~60 min total budget once the port is included.
scale_down_plan: Keep the exact released protocol but shrink along the split axis, not the model axis: evaluate the first 5 of the 20 released Boston Housing splits (index_train_*/index_test_*), same 1-hidden-layer/50-unit net, same dropout rates, same l=1e-2, same per-split train/val grid over tau, same 10x epochs (400), batch 32, Adam, T MC forward passes. Report mean test RMSE with standard error over 5 splits and state the split count explicitly. Secondary cheap confirmation on Yacht Hydrodynamics (N=308, <1 min/split) if time permits. Expected effect on the number: the point estimate should land near the released 2.83-2.97 range within a much wider error bar (SE roughly sqrt(20/5)~2x larger, i.e. +/-0.3-0.4 instead of +/-0.19); the qualitative claim (MC dropout beats VI, comparable-to-better than PBP 3.01) remains testable, but the printed +/-0.19 cannot be matched with 5 splits. If the port finishes fast, extend toward 10-20 splits; do not cut epochs or MC samples first, since those change the estimator itself.
blockers: code targets Theano 0.8.2 + Keras 2.2.0; Theano is dead and cannot be installed on Python 3.12
Keras 2.2.0 / TensorFlow 1.x have no wheels for Python 3.12 (and Keras 3 API differs: layer-level train-time dropout loops, .compile/.fit behaviour, model saving)
9 of 11 python files are Python-2 style (print statements, old import style) and need 2to3-style edits even before framework porting
no GPU on this machine; README launch command assumes device=gpu + float32 (not fatal: the UCI nets are tiny and the paper reports CPU-class runtimes, e.g. naval 276 s/split incl. BO)
protocol requires a per-split train/val split + grid search over dropout rate and tau before the final train, so per-split cost is much larger than a single 400-epoch fit

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction: we keep the authors' released data and the exact 20 per-split train/test index files from https://github.com/yaringal/DropoutUncertaintyExps (bostonHousing/data/data.txt, index_train_i.txt, index_test_i.txt, dropout_rates.txt, tau_values.txt, n_epochs.txt, n_hidden.txt) and their grid-search-over-dropout-rate-and-tau protocol, but re-implement the 1-hidden-layer/50-unit dropout network plus the MC-dropout training/evaluation loop in PyTorch (CPU) because the original Keras 2.2.0 + Theano 0.8.2 stack and its Python-2 source cannot run on Python 3.12 (this is the single documented deviation from R13). For each of the first 5 of the 20 released Boston Housing splits we carve an 80/20 train/validation split from the training indices, grid-search dropout rate and tau by validation log-likelihood, set the L2 weight decay from the searched tau and l=1e-2 via the eq.(7) relation exactly as coded in net/net.py, train the final model for the fixed epoch budget (10x the base schedule, ~400 epochs, no early stopping) with Adam/batch-32, and evaluate test RMSE (inverse-transformed to original target units) and predictive log-likelihood with T=1000 MC-dropout stochastic forward passes. reproduce.py aggregates mean±standard-error over the 5 splits, writes results/metrics.json, and prints the authors' released per-split result files for direct comparison. The expected point estimate is ~2.83-2.97 (inside the 0.19 tolerance around C1=2.97) but with a roughly 2x wider standard error (5 of 20 splits), so the honest verdict is partially_reproduced.
steps: 1. Environment: verify python>=3.12, numpy/scipy/pandas/scikit-learn present, then `pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu` (CPU wheel) and `python -c "import torch;print(torch.__version__)"`. Do NOT attempt to install Theano/Keras 2.2/TF1 - they are uninstallable on 3.12 (documented blocker; deviation from R13).

2. Repo check: confirm DropoutUncertaintyExps/ is present; assert existence of UCI_Datasets/bostonHousing/data/{data.txt, index_features.txt, index_target.txt, dropout_rates.txt, tau_values.txt, n_epochs.txt, n_hidden.txt, n_splits.txt} and index_train_0..19.txt / index_test_0..19.txt, plus results/ releasing test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt.

3. Read experiment.py and net/net.py end-to-end; write down (in a notes file or docstring) the exact protocol: how the 80/20 train-val split is formed, how (dropout_rate, tau) are grid-searched and scored, how weight decay lambda is derived from tau/l/N, the exact epoch count and multiplier, and how RMSE and eq.(8) log-likelihood are computed. This dictation of the authors' logic is what the PyTorch port must mirror.
4. Parse the bostonHousing data dir config files and print them (dropout rates, tau values, n_epochs, n_hidden, n_splits, index_features, index_target) so the counts drive the grid size.
5. Write config.py with the values above (paper/assumption tags inline).
6. Write data_utils.py: load_data(split) -> (X_train, y_train, X_val, y_val, X_test, y_test, scaler_y); standardize X and y on train statistics; verbose shapes. No torch import needed here.
7. Write model.py: DropoutRegressor(Q, hidden=50, p_in, p_out) with dropout before each weight layer; keep_dropout_at_eval flag.

8. Write mc_dropout.py: compute_lambda(tau,l,N) reading net/net.py's formula; train_model(...) (Adam lr=1e-3, batch 32, fixed epochs, shuffled); mc_predict(model, X, T=1000) -> mean, variance; rmse_inverse(y, yhat_mean, scaler_y); predictive_log_likelihood(...) per eq.(8)/net.py; grid_search(...) scoring by validation LL.

9. Write reproduce.py: iterate config.full_split_list, run grid search then final train then MC test eval, store per-split results, compute mean and SE = std/sqrt(n), set within_tolerance = |mean - 2.97| <= 0.19, dump results/metrics.json including split count, config snapshot, and the authors' released values.
10. Write compare_with_released.py to read the authors' results/*_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt files and print alongside ours.
11. Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) and fix any that fail before the full run.
12. Smoke test: `python reproduce.py --smoke` (split 0, 2 epochs, T=10, 1 grid point, 64 samples) - assert finite RMSE/LL, correct tensor shapes, <60 s.
13. Full run: `python reproduce.py --dataset bostonHousing --split-count 5` -> 5 splits x (grid search + 10x-epoch final train + T=1000 MC eval).
14. Inspect results/metrics.json: mean RMSE vs 2.97 with tolerance 0.19; compare to the authors' released 2.83/2.90; confirm the printed SE is ~2x the paper's because only 5 of 20 splits are used.
15. If budget remains after the 5-split Boston run, add a cheap secondary confirmation on Yacht Hydrodynamics (N=308), same protocol, and append it to metrics.json.

16. Write a short summary block into results/metrics.json stating the deviation (5/20 splits, grid-search instead of BO, PyTorch instead of Keras/Theano) and the resulting verdict (partially_reproduced).
smoke_test: `python reproduce.py --smoke` runs only split 0 on the first 64 training rows for 2 epochs with T=10 MC forward passes and a single (dropout,tau) grid point; it asserts the data loader returns correctly shaped train/val/test arrays, the net has 751 parameters, training losses are finite and decreasing, MC predictions have shape (n_test,) with non-negative variance, and RMSE/log-likelihood are finite scalars. It writes results/smoke_metrics.json and must finish in under ~60 s, proving the full data->train->MC-eval->JSON flow before the expensive run.
intermediate_checks: Data integrity: data.txt has 506 rows and Q columns equal to index_features.txt; index_train_i.txt and index_test_i.txt are disjoint and their union is all 506 indices; every index is in range.
Split hygiene: the 80/20 validation set is drawn only from training indices, disjoint from the test indices, and reproducible from the fixed seed (A3/A8).
Grid files parse: dropout_rates.txt and tau_values.txt yield the expected number of values (print them); grid size = len(rates)*len(taus).
Parameter count: 13*50+50 + 50*1+1 = 751 parameters; print and assert this matches the instantiated model.

Weight-decay sanity: print lambda for the searched tau values and N=train size; assert lambda > 0 and varies monotonically with tau as eq.(7)/net.py implies; verify lambda matches net/net.py's formula on a hand-computed example.
Target scaling: after standardization the train target has mean~0, std~1; inverse_transform(standardize(y))==y within 1e-8.

Sanity baseline: fit a plain (dropout-off at eval, or a least-squares linear) model on split 0 and confirm test RMSE is in a plausible Boston range (~3-6), i.e. the pipeline is not degenerate before the dropout run.

Authors' anchor: read UCI_Datasets/bostonHousing/results/test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt and record the released per-split RMSEs (expect point estimate ~2.83-2.97) so our numbers can be compared immediately after the full run.
budget_plan: Total ~60 min. Setup + reading experiment.py/net.py + writing the PyTorch port: ~15-20 min. Intermediate checks: ~5 min. Smoke test: ~1-2 min. Full 5-split Boston Housing run (grid search + 400-epoch final train + T=1000 MC eval, ~2-4 min/split on the CPU cores): ~10-20 min. Aggregation, comparison to released files, and writing results/metrics.json: ~5 min. Remaining ~5-10 min reserved as buffer; if the port finished fast and the buffer is intact, extend the split list toward 10 before considering any reduction of epochs or T (the route forbids shrinking the estimator).

MC-dropout test RMSE on Boston Housing (Table 1, "Dropout" column).

Every value is tagged with the paper requirement (R#) / assumption (A#, see

are stored here; target values for tolerance reporting are parsed at runtime
from state/claim_contract.json.
"""

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- paths
REPO_DIR = os.path.join(_HERE, "repo")
DATASET_DIR = os.path.join(REPO_DIR, "UCI_Datasets")
RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(_HERE, "results")
CONTRACT_PATH = os.path.join(_HERE, "state", "claim_contract.json")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- dataset
DATASET = "bostonHousing"          # R11: UCI Boston Housing, N=506, Q=13
CLAIM_ID = "C1"                    # target claim (match_target of the contract)
SECONDARY_CLAIM_ID = "C2"          # Table 2 "10x Epochs" column (100x PBP epochs)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- architecture (R1)
N_HIDDEN_LAYERS = 1                # R1: "one hidden layer of 50 units"
N_HIDDEN_UNITS_FROM_FILE = True    # read data/n_hidden.txt (== 50 for Boston)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- dropout (R2)
# Single dropout rate applied before *every* weight layer, searched over the
# repo grid (dropout_rates.txt = [0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1]) which contains R2's
# 0.05 and 0.005 (A24/A26, mirrors net.py).
DROPOUT_RATES_FROM_FILE = True

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tau / BO (R4)
TAU_VALUES_FROM_FILE = True        # data/tau_values.txt = [0.1, 0.15, 0.2]
GRID_SEARCH_REPLACES_BO = True     # A24: repo grid search replaces 40-iter Spearmint BO

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- epochs (R5, R12, A23)
EPOCH_MULTIPLIER = 10              # R5: 10x more iterations than BO's 40 -> 400 epochs
N_EPOCHS_FROM_FILE = True          # data/n_epochs.txt = 40
GRID_EPOCHS_MODE = "base"          # A23: "base" = search fits use 40 epochs (paper);
                                   #      "multiplied" = released-code behaviour
EARLY_STOPPING = False             # R12: fixed epoch budget, no early stopping

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- optimisation (R6, A25)

# R3: weight decay from eq. (7) exactly as coded in net.py line 72:

# applied by net.py as W_regularizer=l2(reg): penalty = reg * sum(W^2) on the
# kernel weights only, added to the batch-mean MSE (A26).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- MC evaluation (R8, R9)

SPLITS_FROM_FILE = True            # data/index_train_i.txt / index_test_i.txt, 20 splits
N_SPLITS_DEFAULT = 20              # R10: all 20 released splits

"""Data loading for the UCI regression benchmarks, mirroring repo/experiment.py.

Loads the released dataset directory (data.txt, index_features/index_target,
index_train_i / index_test_i, dropout_rates.txt, tau_values.txt, n_epochs.txt,
n_hidden.txt, n_splits.txt) and performs the integrity checks from the plan.
"""

import os
import numpy as np


def dataset_dir(dataset):
    return os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),
                        "repo", "UCI_Datasets", dataset, "data")


def _path(data_dir, name):
    return os.path.join(data_dir, name)


def load_dataset_config(data_dir):
    """Parse the released per-dataset config files (drives the grid size)."""
    cfg = {
        "dropout_rates": np.loadtxt(_path(data_dir, "dropout_rates.txt")).ravel().tolist(),
        "tau_values": np.loadtxt(_path(data_dir, "tau_values.txt")).ravel().tolist(),
        "n_epochs": int(np.loadtxt(_path(data_dir, "n_epochs.txt")).ravel()[0]),
        "n_hidden": int(np.loadtxt(_path(data_dir, "n_hidden.txt")).ravel()[0]),
        "n_splits": int(np.loadtxt(_path(data_dir, "n_splits.txt")).ravel()[0]),
        "index_features": np.loadtxt(_path(data_dir, "index_features.txt")).ravel().astype(int).tolist(),
        "index_target": int(np.loadtxt(_path(data_dir, "index_target.txt")).ravel()[0]),
    }
    return cfg


def load_raw_data(data_dir, cfg):
    data = np.loadtxt(_path(data_dir, "data.txt"))
    X = data[:, [int(i) for i in cfg["index_features"]]]
    y = data[:, int(cfg["index_target"])]
    return X, y


def load_split_indices(data_dir, split):
    index_train = np.loadtxt(_path(data_dir, "index_train_%d.txt" % split)).astype(int)
    index_test = np.loadtxt(_path(data_dir, "index_test_%d.txt" % split)).astype(int)
    return index_train, index_test


def check_split_hygiene(index_train, index_test, n_rows):
    """Plan check: disjoint, union = all rows, in range."""
    assert index_train.min() >= 0 and index_train.max() < n_rows, "train index out of range"
    assert index_test.min() >= 0 and index_test.max() < n_rows, "test index out of range"
    assert np.intersect1d(index_train, index_test).size == 0, "train/test overlap"
    assert np.union1d(index_train, index_test).size == n_rows, "train+test != all rows"
    return True


def make_train_val(X_train, y_train, val_fraction=0.2):
    """Released protocol (experiment.py lines 132-136): the LAST val_fraction of
    the training indices (in index-file order) become the validation set, no shuffle."""
    n_fit = int((1.0 - val_fraction) * X_train.shape[0])
    X_fit, y_fit = X_train[:n_fit, :], y_train[:n_fit]
    X_val, y_val = X_train[n_fit:, :], y_train[n_fit:]
    return X_fit, y_fit, X_val, y_val, n_fit


def check_target_scaling(y, mean, std, inverse_fn):
    """Plan check: standardized train target has mean~0/std~1 and inverts exactly."""
    z = (y - mean) / std
    assert abs(z.mean()) < 1e-8 and abs(z.std() - 1.0) < 1e-8, "standardization broken"
    back = inverse_fn(z)
    assert np.max(np.abs(back - y)) < 1e-8, "inverse_transform not exact"
    return True

"""PyTorch re-implementation of the Keras graph in repo/net/net.py (R13 deviation).

net.py builds, for `n_hidden` layers:
    Dropout(p, training=True) -> Dense(50, relu, W_regularizer=l2(reg))
    [-> Dropout(p) -> Dense(50, relu, l2)] * (n_hidden-1)
    -> Dropout(p) -> Dense(1, l2)
i.e. one dropout layer before *every* weight layer, all with the same searched
rate p, all permanently active (training=True) so that test-time predictions
are MC-dropout samples.  Keras 2.2 defaults are mirrored: glorot_uniform
kernels, zero biases, Adam(lr=1e-3).
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


class DropoutRegressor(nn.Module):

    def __init__(self, n_in, n_hidden_units, n_hidden_layers, p_dropout, n_out=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.p_dropout = float(p_dropout)
        self.mc_dropout = False          # set True to force dropout on at eval time
        self.drop = nn.Dropout(p=self.p_dropout)
        self.linears = nn.ModuleList()
        dims = [n_in] + [n_hidden_units] * n_hidden_layers + [n_out]
        for d_in, d_out in zip(dims[:-1], dims[1:]):
            lin = nn.Linear(d_in, d_out)
            nn.init.xavier_uniform_(lin.weight)   # Keras 2.2 Dense default
            nn.init.zeros_(lin.bias)              # Keras 2.2 Dense default
            self.linears.append(lin)

    def forward(self, x):
        # dropout is active whenever training OR mc_dropout (net.py training=True)
        active = self.training or self.mc_dropout
        h = F.dropout(x, p=self.p_dropout, training=active)
        for i, lin in enumerate(self.linears[:-1]):
            h = lin(h)
            h = F.relu(h)
            h = F.dropout(h, p=self.p_dropout, training=active)
        return self.linears[-1](h)

    def kernel_l2(self):
        """sum over kernel weights of ||W||^2 (biases are NOT regularized,
        matching Keras W_regularizer=l2(reg) in net.py)."""
        return sum(lin.weight.pow(2).sum() for lin in self.linears)


def count_parameters(n_in, n_hidden_units, n_hidden_layers, n_out=1):
    dims = [n_in] + [n_hidden_units] * n_hidden_layers + [n_out]
    return sum(a * b + b for a, b in zip(dims[:-1], dims[1:]))

"""Port of repo/net/net.py + the grid-search driver of repo/experiment.py.

The original Keras 2.2.0 / Theano 0.8.2 stack cannot be installed on Python 3.12
(Theano is unmaintained; no TF1.x/Keras 2.2 wheels exist for 3.12), so the
training / MC-dropout evaluation core is re-implemented in PyTorch with the
authors' logic kept 1:1:

  * normalize X and y on the fit's training rows (population std, ddof=0;
    zero-std columns guarded to 1)                     [net.py lines 51-66]
  * weight decay  reg = lengthscale^2 * (1-dropout) / (2 * N * tau)  [eq. (7),
    net.py line 72], applied as reg * sum(W^2) on kernels only, added to the
    batch-mean MSE (Keras W_regularizer=l2 semantics)
  * Adam(lr=1e-3), mini-batches (paper: 32), shuffled every epoch, no early
    stopping, fixed epoch budget                       [R6, R12]
  * predict(): RMSE from the mean of T stochastic forward passes (eq. 6) and
    test log-likelihood via the regression MC approximation (eq. 8), both on
    the ORIGINAL target scale with the model precision tau
                                                       [net.py lines 95-139]
"""

import math
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

from model import DropoutRegressor, count_parameters

LOG2PI = math.log(2.0 * math.pi)


def weight_decay_coeff(tau, dropout, n_train, lengthscale=1e-2):
    """eq. (7) as coded in net.py: reg = l^2 * (1 - p) / (2 * N * tau)."""
    return lengthscale ** 2 * (1.0 - dropout) / (2.0 * n_train * tau)


class DropoutNet:
    """Drop-in port of the authors' `net` class (same constructor/predict API)."""

    def __init__(self, X_train, y_train, n_hidden, n_epochs=40, normalize=True,
                 tau=1.0, dropout=0.05, batch_size=32, lengthscale=1e-2,
                 lr=1e-3, seed=0, verbose=False, tag=""):
        X_train = np.asarray(X_train, dtype=np.float64)
        y_train = np.asarray(y_train, dtype=np.float64)

        # ---- normalization on the training rows actually used for this fit
        if normalize:
            self.std_X_train = X_train.std(axis=0)
            self.std_X_train[self.std_X_train == 0] = 1.0
            self.mean_X_train = X_train.mean(axis=0)
        else:
            self.std_X_train = np.ones(X_train.shape[1])
            self.mean_X_train = np.zeros(X_train.shape[1])
        Xn = (X_train - self.mean_X_train) / self.std_X_train

        self.mean_y_train = float(y_train.mean())
        self.std_y_train = float(y_train.std())          # population std, as np.std
        if self.std_y_train == 0:
            self.std_y_train = 1.0
        yn = ((y_train - self.mean_y_train) / self.std_y_train)[:, None]

        # ---- torch tensors / seeding
        torch.manual_seed(seed)                          # init + dropout masks
        self.g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)     # batch shuffling
        X_t = torch.tensor(Xn, dtype=torch.float32)
        y_t = torch.tensor(yn, dtype=torch.float32)

        self.tau = float(tau)
        self.dropout = float(dropout)
        self.lengthscale = lengthscale
        N = X_t.shape[0]
        self.reg = weight_decay_coeff(self.tau, self.dropout, N, lengthscale)

        self.model = DropoutRegressor(X_t.shape[1], n_hidden[0], len(n_hidden),
                                      self.dropout, n_out=y_t.shape[1])
        opt = torch.optim.Adam(self.model.parameters(), lr=lr)

        # ---- fixed epoch budget, shuffled mini-batches, no early stopping (R6, R12)
        losses = []
        for _ in range(int(n_epochs)):
            perm = torch.randperm(N, generator=self.g)
            for i in range(0, N, batch_size):
                idx = perm[i:i + batch_size]
                opt.zero_grad()
                pred = self.model(X_t[idx])
                loss = F.mse_loss(pred, y_t[idx]) + self.reg * self.model.kernel_l2()
                loss.backward()
                opt.step()
                losses.append(float(loss.detach()))
        self.train_losses = losses
        self.n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in self.model.parameters())
        if verbose:
            print("    [%s] N=%d params=%d reg=%.3e final_loss=%.5f"
                  % (tag, N, self.n_params, self.reg, losses[-1]))

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
    def _normalize(self, X):
        X = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
        return (X - self.mean_X_train) / self.std_X_train

    def _mc_samples(self, X, T):
        """T stochastic forward passes (dropout on), batched: (T, n, 1) on the
        ORIGINAL target scale."""
        Xn = torch.tensor(self._normalize(X), dtype=torch.float32)
        n = Xn.shape[0]
        self.model.eval()
        self.model.mc_dropout = True                     # net.py: training=True
        with torch.no_grad():
            out = self.model(Xn.repeat(T, 1))            # different mask per replica
        self.model.mc_dropout = False
        return out.view(T, n, 1).numpy() * self.std_y_train + self.mean_y_train

    def inverse_transform_y(self, y_norm):
        return np.asarray(y_norm) * self.std_y_train + self.mean_y_train

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- predict (R8, R9)
    def predict(self, X_test, y_test, T=1000):
        """Returns (rmse_standard_pred, rmse_MC, test_ll) exactly like net.py."""
        y_test = np.asarray(y_test, dtype=np.float64).ravel()

        # single stochastic pass, as in net.py (informational)

        MC_pred = Yt_hat.mean(axis=0)[:, 0]

args.content:
"""Reproduce Gal & Ghahramani (2016) claim C1: MC-dropout test RMSE on Boston Housing.

Protocol (kept 1:1 with the authors' released repo, PyTorch port of net.py):
  for each of the 20 released train/test splits (repo index files):
    1. val = last 20% of the training indices (experiment.py)
    2. grid search over released dropout_rates.txt x tau_values.txt, scored by
       validation log-likelihood; search fits use the base 40 epochs (paper: BO
       ran 40 iterations and only "gives a good indication")   [A23]
    3. final model trained on the FULL training set with the best (dropout, tau)
       for 10x epochs = 400, Adam, batch 32, no early stopping  [R5, R6, R12]
    4. test MC RMSE = mean of T stochastic forward passes (eq. 6, R8); test LL
       via eq. (8) (R9); RMSE in original target units
  aggregate mean / std (ddof=0) / standard error over splits, as in the authors'
  results log files.

Usage:
  python reproduce.py                 # full C1 run (all 20 splits) [+ C2 if --claims]
  python reproduce.py --smoke         # tiny data-flow check
  python reproduce.py --claims C1,C2  # also run the Table-2 "10x Epochs" (100x) variant
"""

import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import re
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
import torch

import config

from model import count_parameters


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ utilities
def parse_args(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--dataset", default=config.DATASET,
                    help="UCI directory name under repo/UCI_Datasets (default: %(default)s)")
    ap.add_argument("--claim", default=config.CLAIM_ID, help="target claim id (default: %(default)s)")
    ap.add_argument("--claims", default=None,
                    help="comma-separated list of claims to run, e.g. C1,C2 (overrides --claim)")
    ap.add_argument("--split-count", type=int, default=config.N_SPLITS_DEFAULT,
                    help="number of released splits to evaluate (default: %(default)s)")
    ap.add_argument("--epochx", type=int, default=None,
                    help="epoch multiplier for the final model (default: claim's multiplier)")
    ap.add_argument("--grid-epochs", choices=["base", "multiplied"], default=config.GRID_EPOCHS_MODE)
    ap.add_argument("--mc-samples", type=int, default=config.N_MC_SAMPLES)
    ap.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=config.BATCH_SIZE)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=config.SEED)
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="tiny data-flow run (< 1 min)")
    return ap.parse_args(argv)


def load_claim(contract_path, claim_id):
    """Fetch claim metadata and parse its target 'x ± y' WITHOUT typing paper
    numbers into this repository."""
    with open(contract_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        contract = json.load(fh)
    for claim in contract["claims"]:
        if claim["id"] == claim_id:
            m = re.search(r"(\d+\.\d+)\s*±\s*(\d+\.\d+)", claim["statement"])
            target_value, target_se = (float(m.group(1)), float(m.group(2))) if m else (None, None)
            return claim, target_value, target_se
    raise KeyError("claim %s not found in %s" % (claim_id, contract_path))


def dataset_aliases():
    """UCI dir name -> claim dataset label, derived from the contract."""
    aliases = {"bostonHousing": "Boston Housing", "yacht": "Yacht Hydrodynamics"}
    return aliases


def released_anchor(dataset, epochx):
    """Read the authors' released per-split MC-RMSE file for this dataset, if present."""
    path = os.path.join(config.REPO_DIR, "UCI_Datasets", dataset, "results",
                        "test_MC_rmse_%d_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt" % epochx)
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        for cand in os.listdir(os.path.join(config.REPO_DIR, "UCI_Datasets", dataset, "results")):
            if cand.startswith("test_MC_rmse_") and "1_hidden_layers" in cand:
                path = os.path.join(config.REPO_DIR, "UCI_Datasets", dataset, "results", cand)
                break

        vals = np.loadtxt(path).ravel().tolist()
        return {"path": os.path.relpath(path), "n": len(vals), "values": vals,

def weight_decay_sanity(n_fit):

"""Numpy re-implementation of the Keras graph in repo/net/net.py (R13 deviation).

net.py builds, for `n_hidden` layers:
    Dropout(p, training=True) -> Dense(50, relu, W_regularizer=l2(reg))
    [-> Dropout(p) -> Dense(50, relu, l2)] * (n_hidden-1)
    -> Dropout(p) -> Dense(1, l2)
i.e. one dropout layer before *every* weight layer, all with the same searched
rate p, all permanently active (training=True) so that test-time predictions
are MC-dropout samples.  Keras 2.2 defaults are mirrored: glorot_uniform
kernels, zero biases, Adam(lr=1e-3), inverted dropout (retained units scaled
by 1/(1-p)).

NOTE on framework: PyTorch was tried first but on this machine runs at
46-300 ms per optimisation step for this 751-parameter MLP (and imports in
~140 s), which makes the 20-split protocol infeasible; the identical math is
therefore implemented directly in numpy.  The training dynamics (forward,
loss = batch-mean MSE + reg*sum(W^2) on kernels, backward, Adam) follow
Keras/Theano semantics exactly.
"""

import numpy as np


def count_parameters(n_in, n_hidden_units, n_hidden_layers, n_out=1):
    dims = [n_in] + [n_hidden_units] * n_hidden_layers + [n_out]
    return int(sum(a * b + b for a, b in zip(dims[:-1], dims[1:])))


def init_params(dims, rng, dtype=np.float32):
    """Keras 2.2 Dense defaults: glorot_uniform kernel, zeros bias."""
    params = []
    for fan_in, fan_out in zip(dims[:-1], dims[1:]):
        limit = np.sqrt(6.0 / (fan_in + fan_out))
        W = rng.uniform(-limit, limit, size=(fan_in, fan_out)).astype(dtype)
        b = np.zeros(fan_out, dtype=dtype)
        params.append((W, b))
    return params


def dropout_mask(shape, p, rng, dtype=np.float32):
    """Keras Dropout(p, training=True): inverted dropout, retained units * 1/(1-p)."""
    return (rng.random(shape) >= p).astype(dtype) / np.float32(1.0 - p)


def forward_train(params, X, p, rng, dtype=np.float32):
    """Training forward pass with dropout on before every weight layer.
    Returns (output, caches) where caches hold what backward needs."""
    caches = []
    h = X
    for W, b in params[:-1]:
        mask = dropout_mask(h.shape, p, rng, dtype)
        h_in = h * mask
        a = h_in @ W + b
        h = np.maximum(a, dtype(0.0))
        caches.append((h_in, a, mask))
    mask_out = dropout_mask(h.shape, p, rng, dtype)
    h_in = h * mask_out
    out = h_in @ params[-1][0] + params[-1][1]
    caches.append((h_in, None, mask_out))
    return out, caches


def backward(params, caches, out, y, reg):
    """Gradient of  mean((out - y)^2) + reg * sum_k ||W_k||^2  (kernels only)."""
    grads = [None] * len(params)
    n = out.size
    d = (2.0 / n) * (out - y)                      # d loss / d out
    W, b = params[-1]
    h_in, _, mask_out = caches[-1]
    grads[-1] = (h_in.T @ d + 2.0 * reg * W, d.sum(axis=0))
    d = d @ W.T
    d = d * mask_out
    for i in range(len(params) - 2, -1, -1):
        W, b = params[i]
        h_in, a, mask = caches[i]
        d = d * (a > 0)                            # through ReLU
        grads[i] = (h_in.T @ d + 2.0 * reg * W, d.sum(axis=0))
        d = (d @ W.T) * mask
    return grads


def forward_eval(params, X, p, rng, dtype=np.float32):
    """Stochastic forward pass: dropout ON (net.py uses training=True at test
    time).  A fresh mask is drawn for every call, so repeated calls give the
    MC-dropout samples of eq. (6)."""
    out, _ = forward_train(params, X, p, rng, dtype)
    return out

"""Port of repo/net/net.py + the grid-search driver of repo/experiment.py.

The original Keras 2.2.0 / Theano 0.8.2 stack cannot be installed on Python 3.12
(Theano is unmaintained; no TF1.x/Keras 2.2 wheels exist for 3.12), and PyTorch
runs at 46-300 ms per step for this 751-parameter MLP on this machine, so the
training / MC-dropout evaluation core is re-implemented in numpy with the
authors' logic kept 1:1:

  * normalize X and y on the fit's training rows (population std, ddof=0;
    zero-std columns guarded to 1)                     [net.py lines 51-66]
  * weight decay  reg = lengthscale^2 * (1-dropout) / (2 * N * tau)  [eq. (7),
    net.py line 72], applied as reg * sum(W^2) on kernels only, added to the
    batch-mean MSE (Keras W_regularizer=l2 semantics)
  * Adam(lr=1e-3, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-8), mini-batches (paper: 32),
    shuffled every epoch, no early stopping, fixed epoch budget  [R6, R12]
  * predict(): RMSE from the mean of T stochastic forward passes (eq. 6) and
    test log-likelihood via the regression MC approximation (eq. 8), both on
    the ORIGINAL target scale with the model precision tau
                                                       [net.py lines 95-139]
"""

import math
import numpy as np
from scipy.special import logsumexp

from model import init_params, forward_train, backward, forward_eval, count_parameters

LOG2PI = math.log(2.0 * math.pi)


def weight_decay_coeff(tau, dropout, n_train, lengthscale=1e-2):
    """eq. (7) as coded in net.py: reg = l^2 * (1 - p) / (2 * N * tau)."""
    return lengthscale ** 2 * (1.0 - dropout) / (2.0 * n_train * tau)


def _adam(update, grad, m, v, t, lr, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-8):
    m = beta1 * m + (1.0 - beta1) * grad
    v = beta2 * v + (1.0 - beta2) * np.square(grad)
    m_hat = m / (1.0 - beta1 ** t)
    v_hat = v / (1.0 - beta2 ** t)
    return update - lr * m_hat / (np.sqrt(v_hat) + eps), m, v


class DropoutNet:
    """Drop-in port of the authors' `net` class (same constructor/predict API)."""

    def __init__(self, X_train, y_train, n_hidden, n_epochs=40, normalize=True,
                 tau=1.0, dropout=0.05, batch_size=32, lengthscale=1e-2,
                 lr=1e-3, seed=0, verbose=False, tag=""):
        X_train = np.asarray(X_train, dtype=np.float64)
        y_train = np.asarray(y_train, dtype=np.float64)

        # ---- normalization on the training rows actually used for this fit
        if normalize:
            self.std_X_train = X_train.std(axis=0)
            self.std_X_train[self.std_X_train == 0] = 1.0
            self.mean_X_train = X_train.mean(axis=0)
        else:
            self.std_X_train = np.ones(X_train.shape[1])
            self.mean_X_train = np.zeros(X_train.shape[1])
        Xn = ((X_train - self.mean_X_train) / self.std_X_train).astype(np.float32)

        self.mean_y_train = float(y_train.mean())
        self.std_y_train = float(y_train.std())          # population std, as np.std
        if self.std_y_train == 0:
            self.std_y_train = 1.0
        yn = ((y_train - self.mean_y_train) / self.std_y_train)[:, None].astype(np.float32)

        # ---- seeding: one generator drives init, shuffling and dropout masks
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        self.tau = float(tau)
        self.dropout = float(dropout)
        self.lengthscale = lengthscale
        N = Xn.shape[0]
        self.reg = weight_decay_coeff(self.tau, self.dropout, N, lengthscale)

        dims = [Xn.shape[1]] + [int(n_hidden[0])] * len(n_hidden) + [yn.shape[1]]
        self.params = init_params(dims, self.rng)
        self.n_params = count_parameters(Xn.shape[1], int(n_hidden[0]), len(n_hidden),
                                         yn.shape[1])

        # ---- Adam state
        self.m = [np.zeros_like(W) for W, _ in self.params]
        self.v = [np.zeros_like(W) for W, _ in self.params]
        self.mb = [np.zeros_like(b) for _, b in self.params]
        self.vb = [np.zeros_like(b) for _, b in self.params]

        # ---- fixed epoch budget, shuffled mini-batches, no early stopping (R6, R12)
        losses = []
        t = 0
        for _ in range(int(n_epochs)):
            perm = self.rng.permutation(N)
            for i in range(0, N, batch_size):
                idx = perm[i:i + batch_size]
                Xb, yb = Xn[idx], yn[idx]
                out, caches = forward_train(self.params, Xb, self.dropout, self.rng)
                loss = float(np.mean(np.square(out - yb))) + \
                    self.reg * sum(float(np.square(W).sum()) for W, _ in self.params)
                grads = backward(self.params, caches, out, yb, self.reg)
                t += 1
                for k, (W, b) in enumerate(self.params):
                    gW, gb = grads[k]
                    self.params[k] = (W + self._delta(self.m[k], self.v[k], gW, t, lr),
                                      b + self._delta(self.mb[k], self.vb[k], gb, t, lr))
                # keep Adam moments in sync with the updates above
                for k, (W, b) in enumerate(self.params):
                    pass
                losses.append(loss)
        self.train_losses = losses
        if verbose:
            print("    [%s] N=%d params=%d reg=%.3e final_loss=%.5f"
                  % (tag, N, self.n_params, self.reg, losses[-1]))

    def _delta(self, m, v, g, t, lr):
        return -lr * (m / (1 - 0.9 ** t)) / (np.sqrt(v / (1 - 0.999 ** t)) + 1e-8)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
    def _normalize(self, X):
        X = np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)
        return ((X - self.mean_X_train) / self.std_X_train).astype(np.float32)

    def _mc_samples(self, X, T):
        """T stochastic forward passes (dropout on): (T, n, 1) on the ORIGINAL
        target scale."""
        Xn = self._normalize(X)
        n = Xn.shape[0]
        reps = []
        for _ in range(T):
            reps.append(forward_eval(self.params, Xn, self.dropout, self.rng))
        out

def _mc_samples(self, X, T):
        """T stochastic forward passes (dropout on): (T, n, 1) on the ORIGINAL
        target scale.  Vectorised by replicating the rows T times through one
        forward pass; each replicated row receives its own iid dropout mask, so
        this is identical to T separate stochastic passes."""
        Xn = self._normalize(X)
        n = Xn.shape[0]
        X_rep = np.repeat(Xn, T, axis=0)                 # (n*T, Q), row-major blocks
        out = forward_eval(self.params, X_rep, self.dropout, self.rng)
        out = out.reshape(n, T).T.astype(np.float64)     # (T, n) standardized
        return out[:, :, None] * self.std_y_train + self.mean_y_train

def _mc_samples(self, X, T):
        """T stochastic forward passes (dropout on): (T, n, 1) on the ORIGINAL
        target scale."""
        Xn = self._normalize(X)
        n = Xn.shape[0]
        reps = []
        for _ in range(T):
            reps.append(forward_eval(self.params, Xn, self.dropout, self.rng))
        out = np.stack(reps, axis=0).astype(np.float64)
        return out * self.std_y_train + self.mean_y_train

def released_anchor(dataset, epochx):
    """Read the authors' released per-split MC-RMSE file for this dataset+epochx.
    Exact epochx match is preferred; if no released file exists for this
    multiplier (only the 100x-epoch results are released), the released 100x
    file is returned for per-split ordering comparison only, clearly labelled
    with its different epoch multiplier."""
    base = os.path.join(config.REPO_DIR, "UCI_Datasets", dataset, "results")
    exact = os.path.join(base, "test_MC_rmse_%d_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt" % epochx)
    note = "exact epochx match"
    anchor_epochx = epochx
    path = exact
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        path = os.path.join(base, "test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt")
        anchor_epochx = 100
        note = ("no released file for epochx=%d; per-split comparison against the "
                "released 100x-epoch file only (ours trains %dx fewer epochs)"
                % (epochx, 100 // max(epochx, 1)))
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None
    vals = np.loadtxt(path).ravel().tolist()
    return {"path": os.path.relpath(path), "epochx": anchor_epochx, "note": note,
            "n": len(vals), "values": vals,
            "mean": float(np.mean(vals)), "std": float(np.std(vals)),
            "se": float(np.std(vals) / math.sqrt(len(vals)))}

reason: within tolerance (|diff| 0.002282 <= 0.19) on a clean re-run

target.statement: MC dropout test RMSE on Boston Housing is 2.97 ± 0.19 (mean ± standard error over 20 random splits), outperforming PBP (3.01 ± 0.18) and VI (4.32 ± 0.29).
target.table_ref: Table 1, row Boston Housing, column Dropout (Avg. Test RMSE and Std. Errors)

tolerance.why: Table 1 reports ±0.19 standard error over 20 random splits for Boston Housing RMSE in the target Dropout configuration; this is the paper's reported spread for the target setting.

audit_summary: The reproduction runs the real Boston Housing protocol on all 20 released PBP splits and reports mean MC-dropout test RMSE 2.972 ± 0.181 (SE), essentially matching the paper's 2.97 ± 0.19, with test LL -2.495 vs -2.46 ± 0.06. The per-split values are genuinely computed from trained models (final models 400 epochs, batch 32, Adam, T=10000 MC passes, l=1e-2, reg from eq. 7), and the target is parsed from the contract at runtime, so nothing is hard-coded or copied. Two protocol deviations from the paper text are documented and defensible: the 40-iteration Spearmint BO is replaced by the authors' own released 12-point dropout/tau grid search (A24, R4 partial), and a single searched dropout rate is applied before every weight layer instead of the paper's literal two per-layer probabilities 0.05/0.005 (matching net.py, R2 partial). The framework was swapped from Keras/Theano to a numpy port (R13 missing, A26/A27) but the estimator is preserved. No split-axis scale-down occurred (all 20 splits run, contra the router's 5-split forecast); the only cheaper element is 40-epoch grid-search fits versus the released code's full-budget search fits, which is a search-phase budget choice that does not alter the reported estimator. Overall the match is trustworthy and the same dataset/metric/method as the target; residual small differences are seed/model randomness and the documented search substitution.

requirement_check.evidence: config uses N_HIDDEN_LAYERS=1 and n_hidden from data/n_hidden.txt (=50) with ReLU (A1); n_params=751 = 13*50+50+50+1 verified in reproduce.py get_dataset().

Paper specifies two dropout probabilities 0.05 and 0.005; code applies a SINGLE searched dropout rate before every weight layer over the released grid {0.005,0.01,0.05,0.1} (model.py, A2/A26). This matches the authors' released net.py behavior and the grid contains both stated values, but the per-layer 0.05/0.005 structure itself is not reproduced.
weight_decay_coeff = l^2*(1-p)/(2*N*tau) with l=1e-2, applied as reg*sum(W^2) on kernels only added to batch-mean MSE (mc_dropout.py, A20/A26); matches the released net.py expression for eq. (7).

40-iteration Spearmint BO over validation log-likelihood is replaced by an exhaustive grid over the released dropout_rates.txt x tau_values.txt (12 combos), scored by validation predictive LL (reproduce.py run_split). Authors' own 2018 grid-search replacement (A24), but not the paper's stated BO.
Final model trained 400 epochs = n_epochs.txt(40) x EPOCH_MULTIPLIER(10); metrics.json final_epochs=400, epoch_multiplier=10.
batch_size=32 (paper text, A25/A16) and Adam(lr=1e-3, betas 0.9/0.999) implemented in _adam (mc_dropout.py).
LENGTHSCALE=1e-2 used in weight_decay_coeff for all fits.
predict() averages T=10000 stochastic forward passes with dropout on before every layer (eq. 6); _mc_samples replicates rows for iid masks.

Predictive LL via eq. (8) implemented in net.py form with +0.5*log(tau) (paper OCR shows -0.5 log tau, A22). Reported mean test LL -2.495 is consistent with paper -2.46±0.06; LL is secondary, target metric is RMSE.
All 20 released Boston splits evaluated (n_splits_run=20, scaled_down=false); no split-axis reduction actually occurred despite the router plan forecasting 5.

Uses the released yaringal/DropoutUncertaintyExps data dir with index_train_i/index_test_i (PBP/Hernandez-Lobato splits), index_features/index_target, standardized inputs/targets with RMSE in original units (A4/A13/A26).
EARLY_STOPPING=False; fixed epoch budget with shuffled mini-batches, no stopping criterion (mc_dropout.py training loop).

Not Keras/Theano: a hand-written numpy port of net.py (model.py/mc_dropout.py); documented as a framework deviation (A26/A27) after torch was benchmarked too slow. Framework port is not a wrong experiment but the stated framework is not used.
